question: Do ordered intermediate human RGB observations contribute useful physically executed motion beyond endpoints plus a shared supplied robot routine?
claim_ceiling: Video-conditioned projected-appearance retargeting. Not measured human 3D, human motor-action recovery, learned policy or held-out generalisation.

source.missing_values: Unknown; controller holds during brief missing intervals, separately logged.

registration.source_coordinates: dimensionless apparent target-plane projection; not metric when elevated
registration.robot_features: RGB visible orange centroid and directed blue2. Both transformed via robot-camera target-plane homography; direction from two image points.

proxy.status: frozen provisional training proxy, not measured user object; historical catalogue M15 unchanged

timing.event_review: agent visual review of both views; user confirmed correction category, not precise event timestamps
timing.prefix: RGB-localized fixed approach, descend, 20-tick close and clearance lift before source clock. This assistance and timing mismatch is separately logged.

shuffle.boundary_rule: exact boundary samples retained; masks travel with original observations

controller.depth_assumption: Jacobian depth uses supplied nominal horizontal marked-face plane relative to EEF; reference/error is projected appearance, not recovered world pose.
controller.yaw_assumption: top-down wrist, horizontal marked face; actual directed glyph provides yaw correction, not assumed grasp yaw offset

stop_rules: visual feedback unavailable longer than timeout
source reference unavailable longer than timeout

evaluation.ordered_reference_scoring: All conditions scored against original SEQ at the same declared source time; yaw only on supported samples
